title: Build the procedural background renderer and clock
details: Implement a stable 1..20 background catalog and a bounded renderer API for the finalized contracts. Draw only solid axis-aligned rectangles. Derive landscape and portrait clipping from renderer geometry, exclude the well and frame before drawing, and cap all background colors behind HUD at #2A3146. Largest fields stay #0A0C13..#1C2130, secondary shapes at or below #2A3146, accents at or below #8A94AC and at most 2% of the canvas. Support at most 300 small elements or 40 bands per design; document actual emitted primitive and transition costs. Use deterministic cosmetic seeds independent of gameplay randomness. Keep the draw function read-only. Advance a bounded presentation clock without changing simulation timing; pause and focus loss freeze motion and fades, resume has no time jump, and new rounds reset predictably. Implement cuts and visible stepped fades of at most 1s without doubling the draw budget. Support same-session orientation changes with the existing input-clearing boundary. Keep menu backgrounds and letterboxes unchanged; preserve the selected wallpaper beneath pause/game-over overlays. Grayscale mode keeps the wallpaper palette. Off must use the old flat #10121A clear and skip pattern/animation work. Acceptance: meaningful unit and SDL checks cover clipping, independent determinism, clock freeze/reset, integer-step fades, bounds, and orientation. No asset loading, per-frame heap allocation, or unbounded retained state. title: Add saved Auto, Off, and Fixed background options
details: Add a BACKGROUNDS row to OPTIONS and a compact submenu using the existing keyboard and controller menu controls. Provide Background mode Auto/Off/Fixed, default Auto, and Preferred background with every stable ID 1..20 and its name, default 1 Still ground. Changing the preferred ID preserves the mode. Auto follows the current level (clamped 1..20) using the design's transition. Off restores only the old flat #10121A wallpaper, keeps board/grid/frame/HUD/pieces intact, and skips background animation and pattern work. Fixed keeps the selected design across level changes, rounds, and relaunches; level changes must not restart its clock or fade. Fixed backgrounds may animate according to their own contract. Switching to Off or Auto retains the preferred ID. Apply changes on the next play frame in the same session without a restart or new game. Keep names and every menu row readable in both orientations; every ID is reachable with both inputs. Back returns with the cursor on BACKGROUNDS. Save mode and preferred ID atomically on change; extend version-1 canonical settings consistently, accept all valid legacy forms using new defaults, preserve every old preference, reject unknown modes and out-of-range IDs under the established recovery policy, and never write during load. Acceptance: meaningful storage and end-to-end menu scenarios cover both inputs/orientations, Auto boundaries, every Fixed ID, Off, immediate changes, relaunch, corrupted settings, and preference retention. Update specification and player documentation, without changing controls or other options. title: Validate all backgrounds, options, and rendering cost
details: Run integrated acceptance on the full 20-design catalog and saved options, then repair failures. Capture all 40 exact-size orientation views through the real game harness and a 20-level thumbnail sheet. Check emitted commands as well as complete images: base and secondary caps, protected regions, no well/frame writes, accent coverage <=2%, primitive budgets including transitions, static levels 1..4, one moving layer, drift <=10px/s, pulse cycles >=4s, visible stepped fades <=1s, and no abrupt motion resets. Sample intermediate motion and transition phases. Compare normal and grayscale pieces, ghost, and previews against the unchanged background palette. Exercise Auto, Off, every Fixed ID, level cap, restart, pause/resume, focus loss, rapid mode changes, persistence, and repeated orientation changes through keyboard and virtual controller. Identical seed/input replays must keep the same state hashes, scores, and piece sequences in all modes; Off preserves legacy play pixels except the intentional menu additions. Run relevant Debug/Release CTest and harness gates; review intentional new fixtures. Measure worst-case levels 17..20 and transitions in both orientations against Off with the same workload; record draw counts, allocation/memory behavior, CPU, and frame-time percentiles. Host tests must not claim physical RG503 pacing. Update docs and record evidence. Existing T076 owns the final playable visual review and revisions; do not duplicate it or claim player attention was proven by pixel checks. Keep device and release-publication gates unchanged.
